sections.h2: Is a quick sale realistic for a Conroe house?
sections.html:
It is. Owners in Conroe commonly choose between a cash contract that closes in a few weeks and a traditional listing that trades speed for a higher price.

Conroe is where Montgomery County keeps its courthouse, and Interstate 45 runs beside it. Reasons for selling here run from an estate house to a rental with a tenant or a loan that has gone behind.

  • Cash contract: as-is, no open houses, closing on the day you name.
  • Listing: wider buyer pool, but inspections, lender timelines and repair asks.
  • Lease-assigned sale: the buyer steps into an existing tenancy.
  • Pre-auction sale: has to fund before the posted sale day.

sections.h2: How big and how fast-growing is Conroe?
sections.html:
Very. QuickFacts estimates 119,564 residents on July 1, 2025, up 33.0% from an April 2020 base of 89,899. The city's land area went from 52.71 square miles in 2010 to 72.00 in 2020.

sections.h2: Who lives in Conroe and what do they buy?
sections.html:
The same QuickFacts page gives a picture of working households. It counts 39,852 households averaging 2.52 people, with 23.9% of residents under 18 and 13.2% aged 65 or older. Stability is moderate: 82.8% of people kept the same address over the prior year.

  • Veterans: 4,924 residents.
  • Schooling: 87.7% of adults over 25 hold a diploma, and 34.1% have a four-year degree or more.
  • Commute: a mean of 28.6 minutes to work.
  • Broadband: 94.7% of households subscribe.
  • Retail: 2022 retail sales were $4,033,533 thousand, or $39,716 per person, which suggests a regional shopping draw.

A mean commute near half an hour matters to buyers who work in Houston or elsewhere along the interstate, so a house near an on-ramp or a major road tends to draw more questions about travel time.

sections.h2: How did Conroe become the Montgomery County seat?
sections.html:
Houston lumberman Isaac Conroe set up a sawmill in 1881, according to the Texas State Historical Association, and the place was first called Conroe's Switch after its railroad junction. In 1889 Conroe won the county seat from Montgomery and incorporated in 1904 with 1,009 residents.

Oil discovered on December 13, 1931, about seven miles southeast of town, revived a Depression economy and pushed the population to an estimated 5,000 by 1933. Chemical and manufacturing firms later joined the old lumber trade.

Interstate 45 brought Houstonians to the margins of town, and Lake Conroe, impounded in the late 1960s and early 1970s seven miles northwest, added more housing demand. Conroe Independent School District reached its present size of 330 square miles in 1925, so the district extends well past the city line.

sections.h2: What older landmarks and growth stages shaped Conroe?
sections.html:
The same Handbook entry lists details that explain the older core near the courthouse square. Fires in 1901 and 1911 destroyed much of the business district. The State Hotel opened in 1933, the Crighton Theater went up on the square in 1935, and a new courthouse followed in 1936 with a county hospital two years later.

Delta Land and Timber opened one of the South's largest milling operations southwest of town in 1913 and eventually employed 700 people. Conroe's schools were desegregated in 1968, the Montgomery County Library opened in 1946, and a local airfield, built during the war on Farm Road 1484, has served civilian flying since 1945.

Population counts in the entry trace the growth: 27,610 in 1990, 43,617 in 2000 and 63,322 by 2015. The 2025 estimate of 119,564 is almost double that last figure. Houses on the older grid, lake-area homes and new subdivisions all price very differently, so expect a buyer to ask which era yours belongs to.

sections.h2: When do Montgomery County tax bills come due?
sections.html:
Bills are usually mailed in October and are payable on receipt, says the Montgomery County Tax Office. Interest and penalty begin on February 1, and payments count by postmark.

The office prints a penalty of 6 percent at the start, adding a point each month and a last 2 points on July 1, for 12 percent in all, plus 1 percent interest monthly. Partial payments are accepted, though a balance left after January 31 keeps accruing. Call the tax office at (936) 539-7897 or visit 400 N. San Jacinto Street.

Questions about value, exemptions or protests go to Montgomery Central Appraisal District instead. The state deadline to protest is May 15 or 30 days after the notice arrives, whichever falls later.

sections.h2: Who pays the Conroe tax bill when a house sells?
sections.html:
Look at the settlement statement. The tax office advises new owners to check closing papers or call the title company, which may have collected the seller's share and credited the buyer.

One catch: the Comptroller explains the tax lien attaches each January 1 and the owner of that date remains liable. When a lender escrows your taxes, the county suggests writing your loan number on any statement you receive and sending it to the lender.

sections.h2: How does location inside Conroe affect a sale?
sections.html:
Conroe is large, so distance matters. The Handbook places Lake Conroe seven miles northwest of the city and the old oil field seven miles southeast, which gives a sense of the spread. A house near the courthouse square, one near the interstate and one toward the lake attract different buyers, and the 28.6 minute average commute reported by the Census Bureau weighs on all three.

Conroe Independent School District covers 330 square miles, so the campus assigned to a house depends on its address, not only on a Conroe mailing label. Give buyers the exact street address when you ask the district about zoning.

sections.h2: What should a Conroe seller know about exemptions?
sections.html: Homestead status changes what a buyer will owe, so confirm yours is on file. The Comptroller describes a $140,000 school exemption, an extra $60,000 for owners 65 and up or disabled, and a school tax ceiling. Questions about qualifying belong with the appraisal district, as the county tax office itself points out.

sections.h2: What if the Conroe mortgage is behind?
sections.html: Texas foreclosure follows a calendar kept by the State Law Library. Servicers generally wait past 120 days of delinquency, then mail a default notice that leaves 20 days to cure. Auctions are held on a first Tuesday after a posted notice. Closing a sale before that Tuesday keeps the price in your hands, and a lender may still pursue a shortfall for two years after an auction.

sections.h2: What about a tenant or an heir in a Conroe house?
sections.html: Tenants must get written notice, usually three days unless the lease says otherwise, and a contested case goes to justice court. A squatter who was never a tenant is handled under property code chapter 24B through the sheriff or constable. Heirs should have probate, a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or a recorded transfer on death deed in place before a buyer will close.

faqs.a: Montgomery County. Its tax office sits at 400 N. San Jacinto Street in Conroe and answers bill and payment questions.

faqs.q: What date do Conroe taxes turn delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1. The January 31 postmark deadline passes first, and a first-month penalty of 6 percent plus 1 percent interest follows.

faqs.q: Is a Conroe sale possible with taxes unpaid?
faqs.a: It is. The closing agent pays the balance out of your proceeds, so request a tax certificate early to see the exact amount.

faqs.q: Does Montgomery County take part payments?
faqs.a: It does, per the county FAQ. Put the account number on the check with the words partial payment, and expect penalty on any balance left after January 31.

faqs.q: How soon before an auction must a lender send notice?
faqs.a: At least 21 days before the first Tuesday sale, after the 20 day cure period on the default notice has run.
